---
name: localization-architecture
description: How the in-app English ⇄ 中文 language switch and bilingual String Catalog work in SwiftMandarin
metadata:
  type: project
---

**In-app language switch** (added 2026-06-07): The app ships English + Simplified Chinese UI versions, switchable at runtime from Settings WITHOUT changing the device language or relaunching. Core is `Models/LocalizationManager.swift`: an `@Observable @MainActor` singleton with `AppLanguage` enum (`.english="en"`, `.chinese="zh-Hans"`), persisted to UserDefaults key `app_language` (first-launch default follows the system language). The trick: a `Bundle` subclass `LanguageOverrideBundle` is installed once via `object_setClass(Bundle.main, …)`; its `localizedString(forKey:value:table:)` redirects to the user-selected `.lproj` (set via `Bundle.setLanguageOverride(code)` using an associated object). Because SwiftUI resolves every `Text("literal")` / `LocalizedStringKey` through `Bundle.main.localizedString`, this flips ALL string-literal UI live. `SwiftMandarinApp` injects `.environment(\.locale, localization.locale)` and keys the root with `.id(localization.language)` on BOTH the `WindowGroup` and the macOS `Settings` scene so the tree fully re-resolves on switch (caveat: switching resets in-tab navigation state — acceptable for a deliberate, rare action). This is App-Store-safe (public ObjC runtime only, no entitlements). There is also a `@MainActor func L(_ key:)` helper for non-`Text` call sites (services/alerts), but it's rarely needed since literals localize automatically.

**Toggle UI:** a "Language" `Picker` (English / 中文, bound to `$localization.language`) lives in iOS `MoreView → SettingsView` (first section) and macOS `MacOSSettingsView → GeneralSettingsTab` (first section).

**Bilingual String Catalog** (`SwiftMandarin/Localizable.xcstrings`, sourceLanguage `en`, ~549 keys): The app was written with a MIX of `Text("English")` and `Text("中文")` literals, all auto-extracted by Xcode. For a clean two-way switch EVERY key needs BOTH `en` and `zh-Hans`: English-source keys need a `zh-Hans` value; Chinese-source keys (key contains CJK) need an `en` value (else English mode shows Chinese via fallback). Pure-format keys (`%@ · %@`, `→ %@`, `.%@`) need neither (identical in both). Multi-arg strings MUST use positional placeholders (`%1$lld`, `%2$@`) in both languages. Conventions chosen: 词汇本 (vocabulary book, kept — the developer's original term), 您 (formal pronoun, used consistently), brand/tech names untranslated (OpenAI, Ollama, API Key, JSON). Verified via compiled `zh-Hans.lproj` (545 entries) / `en.lproj` (83). A 10-batch+critic Workflow QA'd all entries (0 placeholder errors). The merge was done with a Python script that preserves top-level key order and Xcode's `" : "` 2-space formatting; **NOTE the locale key is `zh-Hans`, not `zh`** (a bug once added stray `zh` entries).

**Non-extracted gap:** `Text(stringVariable)` (e.g. enum `displayName`/`title` returning plain `String`) renders verbatim and does NOT switch. Fixed for the tab bar by adding `AppTab.titleKey: LocalizedStringKey` (used by `ContentView` Tab/sidebar). Intentionally-bilingual enum labels (`LearnerMode.displayName`, `PhotoScanLanguage.displayName`, `TranslationDirection.label` like "EN → 中") are left as-is. Minor known gap: `TranslationDirection.sourceLanguageName/targetLanguageName` ("English"/"Chinese") in History row captions stay English. See [[ai-provider-architecture]] and [[build-and-project-structure]].
